concepts.why: The patient's persistent ulcer and healthy skin patch, combined with genetic testing showing compound heterozygous alterations in COL7A1, support this diagnosis.
The presence of a healthy skin patch with high rates of wild-type transcripts suggests revertant mosaicism in this patient with Epidermolysis Bullosa.
Although less likely, the patient's ulcer and immunofluorescence findings could also be consistent with Junctional Epidermolysis Bullosa.
The patient's skin findings and genetic testing could also be consistent with Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome, although this diagnosis is less likely.
The patient's skin findings could also be consistent with Pseudoxanthoma Elasticum, although this diagnosis is less likely.
The patient's skin findings could also be consistent with Kindler Syndrome, although this diagnosis is less likely.
Although less likely, the patient's ulcer and immunofluorescence findings could also be consistent with Epidermolysis Bullosa Simplex.
The patient's genetic testing and skin findings are consistent with a collagen VII-related disorder.
The presence of dominant RNA transcripts with premature stop codons and rare wild-type reads in affected skin epidermis and dermis explains the persistent ulcer and skin fragility.
